summary: Westport Cove Light, White Bay, Newfoundland: a light from 1906, the octagonal wooden tower of 1911, keepers to about 1989; a seasonal Coast Guard light, tower closed.

lens.note: Sixth-order dioptric lens fitted with the 1911 tower (LF).

light.note: Kerosene until 1969, then solar power (LF). Coast Guard list: seasonal.

structures.note: LF: current tower built 1911; LF also says the tower is only nine feet (about 2.7 m) tall. Coast Guard list and Rowlett: 5.5 m.

staffing.note: LF: four keepers minded the light from 1906 to 1989. The sources read name no current staffing.

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed (LF; Rowlett). LF: 4 km trail from the community wharf, with a steep set of stairs to a picnic area near the light; roughly 0.8 km from the wharf parking area to the light.

events.note: Lens lantern on an open framework, painted white (LF). Rowlett gives 1906 as the establishment year.
Light converted from kerosene to solar power (LF).
End of the keepers' period: LF says four keepers minded the light from 1906 to 1989.

keepers.note: LF: at least 1921. No start date given.

corrections.why: The Coast Guard list gives the structure height as 5.5 m and Rowlett gives 5.5 m (18 ft). The record's 3.0 m comes from Wikidata, which the story does not use as a source. LF's nine feet (about 2.7 m) is the only other figure and is recorded in notes.
LF: the 1906 light was a lens lantern on an open framework; the current wooden octagonal tower was built in 1911. The 1906 date belongs to the first light, which is recorded in facts.light.first_lit.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Three figures: 3.0 m (record, from Wikidata), 5.5 m (Coast Guard list and Rowlett), and nine feet or about 2.7 m (LF). The official list is used: 5.5 m.
The record and Wikidata give the tower as built 1906. LF dates the light 1906 and the current tower 1911, so the year 1906 belongs to the light.

notes_for_editor: Thin station: three sources (LF, the Coast Guard list, Rowlett) agree on the light, the 1911 tower and the 1906 start. LF is the only source for the keepers, the 1911 tower date, the lens, the 1969 solar change and the 1989 end of keepers. LF says four keepers but names three; the story names the three. Heights disagree: 5.5 m (CCG, Rowlett) vs nine feet / about 2.7 m (LF); the story uses 5.5 m. The record's NGA value '110-1140' does not match Rowlett's NGA 1140; possible typo, not changed. The record gives first_lit null; the 1906 first light is from LF and Rowlett. Seasonal operation is from the CCG list and not checked. Canadian Marine reports of 1900 to 1924 do not cover Newfoundland (not part of Canada until 1949), so no primary government report was read. Wikidata and lighthouses.wiki were not used as sources.
